title: Chemical Triphosphorylation of Oligonucleotides
protocol: Prepare the automated DNA/RNA synthesizer with reagents and phosphoramidites according to the target oligonucleotide composition and instrument instructions.
Load a synthesis column containing solid-support onto the synthesizer.
Synthesize oligonucleotides according to the synthesizer instrument protocols.

Remove the 5′-dimethoxytrityl protecting group to yield the solid-supported oligonucleotide 5′-hydroxyl as part of the oligonucleotide synthesis in the previous step or by performing a terminal detritylation step according to the synthesizer instrument protocols.
Remove the column containing the 5′-hydroxyl oligonucleotide on solid support from the synthesizer.
Dry the column under a house vacuum for 10 min to remove residual solvent.
Proceed to triphosphorylation once materials for triphosphorylation are prepared.
If not used immediately, store the dried column under a normal atmosphere in a sealed plastic container with desiccant at -20 °C.
Attach a dry argon source with adjustable pressure to a gas manifold with at least two lines.
Connect the argon source to a bubbler.
Ensure that the lines terminate in 1 mL plastic syringes to facilitate connection to the reaction apparatus.
Gather 1 mL plastic syringes for use during triphosphorylation.
Prepare a three-way polypropylene stopcock for use during triphosphorylation.
Collect noncoring needles for use during triphosphorylation.
Acquire 1.5 mL polypropylene tubes for use during triphosphorylation.
Obtain a small metal spatula for use during triphosphorylation.
Store the gathered equipment in a sealed container or desiccator with desiccant at room temperature for at least 1 day prior to use.
Prepare 30 mL of anhydrous 1,4-dioxane in dried 30 mL glass bottles with drying traps containing 4 Å molecular sieves.
Seal the bottle with rubber septa and store it in a desiccator with desiccant for at least 1 day prior to use.
Prepare 30 mL of 3:1 dioxane:pyridine by volume mixture in dried 7.5 mL glass bottles with drying traps containing 4 Å molecular sieves.
Seal the bottle with rubber septa and store it in a desiccator with desiccant for at least 1 day prior to use.
Prepare 30 mL of N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) in dried 30 mL glass bottles with drying traps containing 4 Å molecular sieves.
Seal the bottle with rubber septa and store it in a desiccator with desiccant for at least 1 day prior to use.
Prepare 30 mL of acetonitrile (ACN) in dried 30 mL glass bottles with drying traps containing 4 Å molecular sieves.
Seal the bottle with rubber septa and store it in a desiccator with desiccant for at least 1 day prior to use.
Store solid 2-chloro-4H-1,3,2-benzodioxaphosphorin-4-one (salicyl phosphorochloridite, SalPCl) in its original container inside a sealed jar with desiccant at 4 °C.
Always flush the container with argon between uses before opening.
Prepare a tributylammonium pyrophosphate (TBAP) solution at least 5 days in advance of the triphosphorylation reaction: weigh solid TBAP in a dried 30-mL glass bottle.
Dissolve 1-5 g of solid TBAP in 1 mL of DMF and 0.5 mL of tributylamine per g of TBAP.
Add three drying traps to the solution.
Seal the bottle with a rubber septum under argon.
Bubble the sealed bottle with argon for 30 min to degas.
Store inside a sealed jar with desiccant at 4 °C for 5 days.
Retrieve the synthesis column and allow it to warm to room temperature if stored at -20 °C.
Prepare the antechamber by removing the plunger from a dry 1 mL syringe.
Cut off the top of the syringe using scissors or a razor blade.
Attach the prepared syringe to the synthesis column.
Attach a three-way stopcock to the top of the syringe.
Connect the side inlet of the stopcock to the dry argon source with the bubbler.
Secure this apparatus to a stand with clamps.
Seal all upstream joints with wax sealing film.
Adjust the stopcock so that the injection port is closed and the apparatus is open to the argon source.
Close the bubbler, and allow argon at low pressure (<10 psi) to stream through the reaction chamber for 5 min.
Reopen the bubbler and attach a syringe to the bottom of the synthesis column as the waste syringe.
Pull argon through the column repeatedly using the waste syringe.
Retighten the waste syringe with the plunger pushed fully in.
Set the stopcock so that the injection port is closed and the apparatus is open to the argon source.
Attach a needle to the dry argon source and insert it into the reagent or solvent bottle septum carefully.
Avoid immersing the needle in the bottle contents.
Assemble a dry syringe with a needle.
Insert the needle into the reagent or solvent bottle septum without immersing it into the bottle contents.
Fill the syringe with argon, withdraw the needle from the septum, and expel the argon.
Repeat filling the syringe with argon and expelling it again.
Fill the syringe with the required volume of solvent or reagent under argon pressure.
Adjust the stopcock on the apparatus to close the argon source and open the injection port.
Quickly remove the filled syringe and needle from the source bottle, wipe away any solvent stuck to the side or tip of the needle.
Insert the needle into the injection port and expel the reagent into the antechamber of the apparatus.
Remove the needle and close the injection port, reopening the apparatus to the argon source.
Gently draw the liquid from the antechamber all the way through the synthesis column using the waste syringe.
Ensure all liquid is now held in the waste syringe.
Slowly push the solution back up into the synthesis column, ensuring no gas bubbles are in the column.
To mix or agitate, gently pull the solution up and down over the column with the waste syringe.
Slowly pull the solution into the waste syringe.
After the bulk of the solution has passed into the waste syringe, pull argon through to flush the remaining solvent from the column.
Remove the wax sealing film around the waste syringe joint.
Remove the waste syringe and discard the waste solution.
Replace the waste syringe with a new, dry syringe.
Re-seal the joint with wax sealing film.
Add 200 µL of pyridine/dioxane to the antechamber.
Weigh 6-12 mg of SalPCl into a dry microcentrifuge tube.
Dissolve SalPCl in 100 µL of dioxane by gently syringing.
Add dissolved SalPCl to the antechamber and load onto the synthesis column.
React for 15 min, agitating every 5 min.
Remove and discard the SalPCl solution.
Add 250 µL of TBAP solution to the antechamber and load onto the synthesis column.
React for 20 min, agitating every 5 min.
Remove and discard the TBAP solution.
Wash the column with 0.5 mL of DMF, removing the solvent after addition.
Wash the column with 0.5 mL of ACN, removing the solvent after addition.
Add 250 µL of oxidizer solution to the antechamber and load onto the synthesis column.
React for 30 min, agitating every 10 min.
Remove and discard the oxidizer solution.
Wash the column with 0.5 mL of ACN.
Disassemble the reaction apparatus.
Wash the synthesis column with 5 mL of ACN.
Dry the column.
Transfer the dried solid support resin to a 1.5 mL polypropylene screw-cap sealable tube with a silicone o-ring.
Suspend the resin in 1 mL of a 1:1 mixture of 28%-30% aqueous ammonia and 40% aqueous methylamine (AMA).
Seal the tube tightly.
Incubate at 65 °C for 10 min with intermittent mixing by gentle inversion.
Chill the tube on ice.
Briefly centrifuge it at 6,000-12,000 × g for 10 s.
Remove the supernatant from the resin.
Filter through a syringe equipped with a 0.2 µm filter.
Transfer the filtrate to a new, sterile polypropylene tube.
Evaporate the solution to dryness using a vacuum centrifuge fitted with an ammonia-neutralizing chemical trap.
Dissolve dried material in 1 mL of 1 M tetrabutylammonium fluoride (TBAF) in THF if RNA nucleotides contain silyl protecting groups.
Heat the TBAF solution to 55 °C and shake as necessary until fully dissolved.
Incubate at room temperature for 16-24 h to remove silyl protecting groups.
Quench the TBAF solution with 1 mL of 1 M Tris buffer, pH 7.5.
Remove THF using a vacuum centrifuge.
Remove TBAF salts using a disposable size exclusion column according to manufacturer's instructions.
Collect eluate in fractions and identify main product fractions by absorbance at 260 nm for oligonucleotides shorter than 15 nt.
Concentrate the deprotected RNA oligonucleotide by lyophilization or vacuum centrifuge if less than 15 nt, or by ethanol precipitation if greater than 15 nt.
Prepare a preparative scale 10%-20% polyacrylamide/8 M urea/1x TBE gel using 19:1 mono:bis acrylamide stock.
Assemble the gel plate in the gel stand with 1x TBE in reservoirs.
Pre-run the gel at 35 W for at least 30 min.
Dissolve solid oligonucleotide in urea gel loading buffer and heat to 80 °C.
Load the dissolved oligonucleotide onto the polyacrylamide gel.
Run the gel for 1-2 h at 25-35 W.
Remove the gel plate from the gel stand after electrophoresis is complete.
Disassemble the gel plate.
Wrap the gel in polyvinylchloride film.
Identify product bands by back-shadowing with 254 nm UV light.
Excise the major product band using a razor blade.
Crush the excised gel through a plastic syringe or mechanically.
Elute in 3x volumes of crush and soak buffer (300 mM NaCl; 10 mM Tris, pH 8; 1 mM EDTA) for at least 12 h with agitation or shaking.
Remove solid gel pieces by passing the solution through a syringe fitted with a 0.2 µm filter.
Concentrate the oligonucleotide by ethanol precipitation.
For oligonucleotides shorter than 15 nt, elute in 3x volumes of nuclease-free water for at least 12 h with agitation or shaking.
Remove solid gel pieces by passing the solution through a syringe fitted with a 0.2 µm filter.
Concentrate by lyophilization.
Remove residual salts and solutes using a disposable size exclusion column as in step 5.6.
Concentrate by lyophilization.
Store purified triphosphorylated oligonucleotides at -20 °C in TE buffer (10 mM Tris, pH 8; 1 mM EDTA).
Determine the concentration of the oligonucleotide by measuring the absorbance at 260 nm using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Verify triphosphorylation by mass spectrometry.
Look for an expected mass of +239.94 Da relative to that of the 5′-hydroxyl oligonucleotide.
Prepare solution A as a mixture of self-replicator ribozyme E and 5′-32P-labeled RNA substrate A14 to concentrations of 0.30 µM and 30 µM, respectively.
Prepare solutions B-transcribed and B-synthetic with 15 µM triphosphorylated RNA substrate B prepared by in vitro transcription or chemical triphosphorylation as above, respectively.
Bring both solutions to 42 °C.
Rapidly mix 5 μL of solution A with 10 μL of solution B-transcribed or B-synthetic to a final concentration of 0.1 µM E, 10 µM A, 10 µM B, 25 mM MgCl2, and 50 mM EPPS buffer at pH 8.5.
Incubate the reaction mixture at 42 °C.
Take 0.5 μL aliquots and quench in 9.5 μL of formamide gel loading buffer (95% formamide; 10 mM EDTA, pH 8).
Prepare an analytical polyacrylamide/8 M urea/1x TBE gel according to the appropriate protocol.
Assemble the cast gel and plate it in a gel stand.
Fill the reservoirs with 1x TBE and prerun at 40 W for 30 min (or as appropriate).
Heat the quenched reaction samples to 80 °C.
Load 5 μL of the sample into each well.
Run the gel at 40 W for approximately 40 min (or as appropriate).
Remove the gel plate from the gel stand and disassemble it.
Wrap the gel in polyvinylchloride film.
Cover the gel with a phosphor screen and expose it for 1 h (or as appropriate for 32P cpm).
Scan the screen using a fluorescent/phosphorescent gel scanner.
Quantify the reaction yield using gel image quantification software.
Choose Analysis | Background Subtraction.
Select Areas | the rectangle shape.
Draw a rectangle of the same size in an empty portion of the gel image.
Change the background subtraction method for all rectangles to Image Rectangle.
Choose Window | 2 Area Window.
Edit | Export to Excel to export quantified band pixel volumes to a spreadsheet file.
Plot the concentration of product E versus time.
Fit the data to the logistic growth Eq (1) using statistical data-fitting software.
In the exported spreadsheet, divide the product E volume by the sum of substrate A and product E volumes to determine the fractional yield of product for each time and both reactions.
Multiply by the initial concentration of substrate A (10 µM) to determine the yield of product E as a function of time.
Choose File | New | New Project File in statistical data-fitting software.
Select XY under New Table & Graph, and click Create.
Enter the reaction times and product E yields for both reactions in adjacent columns.
Label columns correspondingly (e.g., "time", "transcribed B", "synthetic B").
Choose Insert | New Analysis.
Select XY analyses | Nonlinear regression (curve fit).
Click OK.
Choose Growth curves | Logistic growth.
Click OK.
Observe the fit parameters and confidence intervals under Results.
Observe the plot of data points and fitted curves under Graphs.

Prepare 10 µL of RNA solution containing 20 µM D-RNA 27.3t cross-chiral polymerase, 2 µM 5′-fluorescein-labeled L-RNA primer, 4 µM biotinylated L-RNA hammerhead template, and 20 µM each of L-RNA pppCUG, pppAUG, pppAGG, and pppCGC.
Anneal the RNA by heating it to 90 °C for 1 min.
Cool the annealed RNA to 23 °C at 0.2 °C/s in a PCR thermocycler.
Incubate the RNA solution at 17 °C.
Start the reaction by adding 10 µL of 2x start buffer (400 mM MgCl2, 500 mM NaCl, and 50 mM Tris, pH 8.3).
Take 10 µL aliquots as the reaction proceeds.
Quench each aliquot with 5 µL of 0.5 M EDTA, pH 8.
To each quenched reaction sample, add 0.1 mg of streptavidin-coated magnetic beads suspended in 10 μL of 1 M NaCl in TE buffer with 0.05% neutral detergent.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min at room temperature with shaking.
Capture the beads on a bead-capture magnet and remove the liquid.
Add 50 μL of wash solution (250 mM NaCl in TE with 0.05% neutral detergent).
Mix the beads, capture them again, and discard the wash solution.
Repeat the washing step once more.
To elute extended primers from beads, add 50 μL of elution solution (25 mM NaOH with 0.05% neutral detergent).
Mix the beads thoroughly.
Recapture the beads and remove the elution solution.
Quench with 100 mM Tris (pH 7.5) and precipitate with ethanol.
Dissolve the precipitated RNA in 10 μL of formamide gel loading buffer.
Prepare unreacted end-labeled primer at 0.5 µM in formamide gel loading buffer.
Heat samples to 80 °C.
Load 5 μL of each sample into a well on an analytical polyacrylamide/8 M urea/1x TBE gel.
Prerun the gel at 40 W for 30 min (or as appropriate).
Run the gel at 40 W for approximately 40 min.
Remove the gel plate from the stand.
Scan the gel plate using a fluorescent/phosphorescent gel scanner to visualize cross-chiral L-RNA extension products.
